summary_paragraph: A pregnant patient with a history of bipolar disorder and borderline personality disorder was admitted due to severe depression with psychotic features and suicidal ideation. She reported feeling stiff, restless, and emotionally overwhelmed. During her hospitalization, she was found to have hyponatremia and acidosis, which were managed with careful fluid correction. Hypothyroidism and anemia were diagnosed and treated with appropriate supplementation. Her asthma and GERD were managed with ongoing medications. After limited response to pharmacotherapy, she underwent a single session of unilateral electroconvulsive therapy, which led to significant improvement in mood and cognition. Suicidal thoughts resolved, and she was discharged with a revised medication regimen, including antidepressants, thyroid replacement, and iron, along with close psychiatric follow-up. She expressed hope and readiness to continue recovery at home.
